title: Confinement transitions in half-space constrained Riesz gases
authors: Sung-Soo Byun, Yong-Woo Lee, Eui Yoo
abstract: We study a Riesz gas with interaction parameter $s \in (d-3,d)$ in an arbitrary spatial dimension $d$, confined to a half-space by a hard wall. We prove that the equilibrium measure exhibits a dichotomy according to the interaction range. For $s \in (d-2,d)$, corresponding to the weakly long-ranged regime, the equilibrium measure always retains a non-trivial bulk component and thus is never completely confined to the wall. In contrast, for $s \in (d-3,d-2]$, corresponding to the strongly long-ranged regime, a confinement transition occurs: there exists a critical wall position beyond which the equilibrium measure is supported entirely on the wall. Our theorem generalises recent results established for the Coulomb gas, corresponding to the case $s=d-2$.
summary: This paper analyzes the equilibrium state of a Riesz gas confined to a half-space. It proves that the system's behavior undergoes a sharp transition depending on the interaction strength $s$. Specifically, it identifies a critical wall position beyond which the particles are forced entirely onto the boundary for strongly long-ranged interactions.
main_problem: The study investigates how the equilibrium state of a Riesz gas changes when confined to a half-space, specifically determining if this confinement exhibits qualitative transitions based on the interaction range.
main_result: A dichotomy exists: for weakly long-ranged interactions ($s \in (d-2, d)$), the measure always has bulk support; however, for strongly long-ranged interactions ($s \in (d-3, d-2]$), a critical wall position $a_{crit}$ dictates whether the system is fully confined to the wall.
method: The analysis uses variational methods by minimizing an energy functional and proving necessary conditions via Euler–Lagrange inequalities applied to the constrained equilibrium measure.
model_or_system: The model is a Riesz gas with interaction parameter $s \in (d-3, d)$ in dimension $d$, confined to a half-space by a hard wall. The energy functional involves the Riesz kernel $g_s(x)$.
key_observables: The nature of the equilibrium measure $\mu_a$: whether it retains non-trivial bulk support or becomes entirely supported on the confining wall.
important_parameters: Interaction exponent $s$, dimension $d$, and the critical wall position $a_{crit}(d, s)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to $s \in (d-3, d)$; specific mathematical tools like the incomplete beta function and properties of Gauss hypergeometric functions are employed.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate particle configurations showing non-confinement in the weakly long-ranged regime and demonstrating full confinement at a critical wall position in the strongly long-ranged regime.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by defining the energy functional, then proves the dichotomy theorem (Theorem 2.2) by analyzing the Euler–Lagrange inequality across different regimes of $s$, culminating in rigorous proofs for confinement conditions.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, understanding phase transitions and critical thresholds in interacting particle systems is fundamental to many-body physics, including quantum gas models where effective interactions can be long-ranged.
